Reconstruct visible diagram linework and arrows, headed or headless: connectors, internal wiring, dense networks, graph edges, axes, baselines, separators, brackets, dimensions, callout leader lines and legend lines. Exclude the outlines of closed NON-ARROW shapes: rectangles, rounded rectangles, circles, ellipses, polygons, and closed frames or containers, whether solid or dashed. These belong to shape reconstruction. Do not reconstruct their individual sides or nominate their borders as missing lines, even when a crop or mask contains only part of the outline. A grid made of adjacent closed cells is ONE composite shape: exclude both its outer border and internal shared cell edges; do not split it into independent lines or nominate those edges as missing. Use whole-figure context to distinguish shape components from independent lines. Connectors between distinct objects remain eligible, including dense networks; a connector forming a loop is not automatically a shape outline. Being inside a module, being dense, or lacking an arrowhead is NOT a reason to exclude a line. Broad block arrows remain eligible as closed arrow shapes with fill and stroke. Exclude text/glyph strokes and photographic texture. Do not duplicate an object explicitly supplied as already reconstructed; a box or a SAM mask alone does not prove coverage. Follow the visible strokes and attachments; never assume all-to-all connections or extend wires through opaque objects. Crossings alone are not junctions. SAM candidates are fallible evidence, not proof of eligibility.
